title: Measurement: Length
description: Class 3 Length: units (mm, cm, m, km), measuring with a ruler, comparing lengths, and converting metres to centimetres and kilometres to metres — with worked examples and tests.

topics.title: Units of Length
topics.concept:
We measure how long something is using units. From small to big:

  • millimetre (mm) — very tiny, like the thickness of a coin.
  • centimetre (cm) — your finger is about 1 cm wide.
  • metre (m) — about the height of a door handle from the floor.
  • kilometre (km) — a long distance you walk or drive.

We use a ruler to measure short lengths in cm and mm.

examples.problem: Which unit best measures the length of a pencil?
examples.solution: Centimetres (cm) — a pencil is about 15 cm long.

examples.problem: Which unit best measures the distance between two cities?

recap: Units of length from small to big: mm, cm, m, km.
Use cm for small objects, m for a room, km for long distances.
A ruler measures short lengths in centimetres and millimetres.

topics.title: Comparing & Converting Length
topics.concept:
Useful conversions to remember:

  • 1 cm = 10 mm
  • 1 m = 100 cm
  • 1 km = 1000 m

To change metres to centimetres, multiply by 100. To compare two lengths, make them the same unit first.

examples.problem: Which is longer: 2 m or 150 cm?
examples.solution: 2 m = 200 cm, and 200 cm > 150 cm, so 2 m is longer.

recap: To compare lengths, change them to the same unit first.
